title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 653–655 of the 'suite à la Longue Marche'). S is a reduced integral scheme, G a group scheme over S, and g ∈ G(S) a section. The proposition being proved is a criterion for g to lie, up to a power, on an additive one-parameter subgroup: there should exist n>0 and a homomorphism φ: G_a → G with φ(1)=g^n. The group must be G_a, not G_m as the transcription says; see the corrections.

Sufficiency is trivial. For necessity, the previous page splits into two cases.
- (a) g_η has finite order (residue/generic characteristic p): then g^n=1 and φ is trivial.
- (b) Generic characteristic 0, g_η unipotent: there is a unique φ_{1η}: G_{a,η} → G_η with φ_{1η}(1)=g_η, given by the logarithm. Let U_1 be its open of definition. Put φ_{nη}(λ)=φ_{1η}(nλ), with open of definition U_n.

This page.
- (16): n | n' ⇒ U_n ⊂ U_{n'}, since φ_{n'} = φ_n((n'/n)·).
- The goal is ⋃U_n = S. One reduces to S local with φ_1 defined on the punctured spectrum U_1 = S∖{s} (17).
- This becomes a Lemma(?): let S be normal integral, G locally of finite presentation, U ⊂ S a nonempty open, φ_U: G_{a,U} → G_U a homomorphism, and suppose φ_U(1) extends to a section g of G over S. There is a parenthetical, partly illegible, saying the case G affine (resp. a faithful-representation reduction?) follows from general results of SGA 3. Conclusion: for some n>0, λ ↦ φ_U(nλ) extends to a homomorphism φ_n: G_a → G over S.
- Grothendieck declines the general proof. As a 'decisive test' he treats G = GL_N over a regular scheme of dimension 1, i.e. a DVR (or Dedekind ring) A with fraction field K.
- Next page (18)–(19): X ∈ M_N(K) nilpotent with exp(±X) ∈ M_N(A); want d>0 with d^i X^i/i! ∈ M_N(A) for 1 ≤ i ≤ N−1.
- If A is a Q-algebra, the logarithm X = log(1+Y), with Y = exp X − 1, shows X itself is integral, so φ_1 already extends.
- In mixed characteristic p, d can be taken a power of p. Hence the corollary: if φ is defined on an open containing S∖V(p), then φ^{p^ν} extends.

The purpose is a local-to-global extension statement for exponentials/one-parameter unipotent subgroups. It is presumably needed in the surrounding Galois-theoretic or schematic-group discussion of the Longue Marche (unipotent elements, 'schematisation' of discrete groups).
errors: Read literally, the transcription's G_m is inconsistent: a homomorphism G_m → G sends 1 to the identity, and φ_n(λ)=φ_1(nλ) together with the exponential on the next page show the group must be G_a.

The general Lemma is asserted without proof and some hypotheses are needed. Normality of S is essential (non-normal bases fail). Some separatedness or affineness of G is presumably also needed: with non-separated group schemes, extension of homomorphisms can fail or be non-unique. Grothendieck himself only tests GL_N over a DVR.

The GL_N/DVR test case is correct. X = log(1+Y) = Σ_{i<N} (−1)^{i+1} Y^i/i, with Y integral and nilpotent, so lcm(1,…,N−1)·X is integral. Then d = lcm(1..N−1)·(N−1)! works, and only primes < N enter. In residue characteristic 0, X itself is integral. No error, only the gap of the general case.

ideas.what: Criterion: a section g of a group scheme over a reduced integral base has a power lying on an additive one-parameter subgroup G_a → G iff the generic fibre is unipotent or of finite order. The proof spreads out the logarithm's domain of definition by passing to multiples nλ.
ideas.modern_name: Integral exponential/logarithm of unipotent elements; extension of one-parameter unipotent subgroups over normal bases
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; exponentials of unipotents over Z_(p) studied by Serre, Seitz, McNinch, Balaji–Deligne–Parameswaran (char p, p ≥ Coxeter number)
ideas.where_published: Not in SGA 3 in this form as far as I know; SGA 3 treats extension of homomorphisms of tori and multiplicative groups, not G_a

ideas.what: Lemma: over normal integral S, a homomorphism φ_U: G_{a,U} → G_U whose value at 1 extends to S has some multiple λ ↦ φ_U(nλ) extending over S. Only powers of p are needed if U ⊃ S∖V(p).
ideas.modern_name: Extension of homomorphisms G_a → G after rescaling (Hartogs-type extension for unipotent one-parameter subgroups)

ideas.what: Test case: N×N nilpotent X over K with exp(±X) integral implies d^i X^i/i! integral for some d, using only primes < N; in residue char 0, X itself is integral, via log.
ideas.modern_name: Integrality of log of unipotent matrices / divided powers of nilpotent matrices

missed.claim: Grothendieck states but explicitly refuses to prove a general extension lemma for one-parameter additive subgroups (G locally of finite presentation over normal integral S). He verifies only GL_N over a DVR.
missed.quote: Je ne vais pas essayer de le démontrer dans ce contexte général des schémas en groupes généraux, et vais me limiter, à titre de test décisif ... au cas où G = GL(n)_S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. For affine flat G it reduces quickly to GL_N via a closed embedding plus normality. It is a small, essentially routine open end; the precise hypotheses (separatedness, normality) are not spelled out.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine technical lemma (integrality of logarithms of unipotent elements, extension after rescaling), correctly handled in the test case. Nothing here seems absent from or significant for the literature.
transcription_corrections: Read G_a (additive group) instead of G_m throughout, e.g. 'φ_U : G_{a,U} → G_U' and 'φ_n : G_a → G'.
'φ_U^n : λ ↦ φ_U(λ^n)' should be 'λ ↦ φ_U(nλ)' (additive rescaling), consistent with the previous page's φ_{nη}(λ)=φ_{1η}(nλ).
'H entier' is likely 'G affine' (or 'G entier'); the parenthetical seems to refer to reducing, via general SGA 3 results, to the case of a (faithful) representation.
'S du plus [?] régulier de dim 1' plausibly reads 'S de plus supposé régulier de dim 1'.
'(pour importantes conviction que je sache)' is plausibly '(pour me faire une conviction ...)'; it is illegible in part.
